description: EES (Explicit Estimation Search) finds a path that costs at most `w` times the optimum. It uses three estimates: an *admissible* heuristic `h` (it never overestimates), which proves the bound; a more accurate cost estimate `ĥ`, which may overestimate; and `d̂`, an estimate of the number of steps to the goal. Its first choice is the open state with the smallest `d̂` among those with `f̂ = g + ĥ ≤ w · f̂_min`. It takes that state only if its `f̂` is at most `w · f_min`, with `f = g + h`; else it takes the state with the smallest `f̂` under the same test, and else the state with the smallest `f`, which raises `f_min`. Use it when solution cost and solution length differ and you have good estimates of both.

papers.title: Bounded Suboptimal Search: A Direct Approach Using Inadmissible Estimates
papers.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI)
